title: RLS-12L: robust low-bit sieve with 12 ceil(log2 n) stages, O(2^(n/(12 log2 n)) n^41/log2 n) work, adaptive malformed-copy tolerance 1/(16384n^12)

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N) and L = log2 n, the RLS-12L algorithm (robust low-bit sieve with 12 ceil(log2 n) stages) with the single parameter rule of proof.md Section 4 (for n >= 524288: at most R = 12 ceil(log2 n) stages per round, b = ceil((n-1)/R) bits per stage, M = R 2^(b+2R+6) leaves per round, G = 2^(R+9) grid guesses, k = 64 bitlength(100G) test copies per guess, Q = G(nM + k) copies all acquired before the first measurement, r1 = 200 bitlength(1600(n+1)Q), sort keys of 2 bitlength(Q) + 10 bits; for n < 524288 the robust exhaustive branch of Section 6.8 with 2^26 copies per candidate) has worst-case total work T(N,s) = O(2^(n/(12 log2 n)) n^41 / log2 n) in the challenge cost model (all classical bit operations, circuit generation, gates, measurements, initialisation, sorting, the address charge ceil(log2(𝔐+2)) = O(n/log2 n) per counted operation where 𝔐 = O(2^(n/(12 log2 n)) n^38 log2 n) (proof.md Section 1) is the number of allocated bits plus qubits, and n+1 per acquired copy; dominated by label estimation, O(n^4/(log2 n)^2) per leaf over at most Q leaves, where Q < 2^56 n^37 (log2 n) 2^(n/(12 log2 n)) for n >= 524288; proof.md Section 8), i.e. uniform envelope B_T(n) = 2^(n/(12 log2 n)) n^41 (log2 n)^(-1), whose growth index is exactly 1 (proof.md Section 9). This holds on every execution branch, for the clean problem and for every adversary of the error model of the fifth claim, jointly with the other three resource bounds and full-secret success probability at least 9/10 (> 2/3) of the same algorithm and configuration (proof.md Theorems 1 and 2). All constants are absolute (independent of N, s, the adversary and all outcomes); inputs with n < 524288 are finitely many values of N with constant cost.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N) and L = log2 n, the RLS-12L algorithm (robust low-bit sieve with 12 ceil(log2 n) stages) with the single parameter rule of proof.md Section 4 (for n >= 524288: at most R = 12 ceil(log2 n) stages per round, b = ceil((n-1)/R) bits per stage, M = R 2^(b+2R+6) leaves per round, G = 2^(R+9) grid guesses, k = 64 bitlength(100G) test copies per guess, Q = G(nM + k) copies all acquired before the first measurement, r1 = 200 bitlength(1600(n+1)Q), sort keys of 2 bitlength(Q) + 10 bits; for n < 524288 the robust exhaustive branch of Section 6.8 with 2^26 copies per candidate) has worst-case peak classical space S_C(N,s) = O(2^(n/(12 log2 n)) n^38) bits (sort keys and the rank table, O(Q n/log2 n) bits, which dominate the current round's M records, the 2^b key counters and the O(n^2) controller; proof.md Section 8), i.e. envelope B_C(n) = 2^(n/(12 log2 n)) n^38, whose growth index is exactly 1. This holds on every execution branch, for the clean problem and for every adversary of the error model of the fifth claim, jointly with the other three resource bounds and full-secret success probability at least 9/10 (> 2/3) of the same algorithm and configuration (proof.md Theorems 1 and 2). All constants are absolute (independent of N, s, the adversary and all outcomes); inputs with n < 524288 are finitely many values of N with constant cost.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N) and L = log2 n, the RLS-12L algorithm (robust low-bit sieve with 12 ceil(log2 n) stages) with the single parameter rule of proof.md Section 4 (for n >= 524288: at most R = 12 ceil(log2 n) stages per round, b = ceil((n-1)/R) bits per stage, M = R 2^(b+2R+6) leaves per round, G = 2^(R+9) grid guesses, k = 64 bitlength(100G) test copies per guess, Q = G(nM + k) copies all acquired before the first measurement, r1 = 200 bitlength(1600(n+1)Q), sort keys of 2 bitlength(Q) + 10 bits; for n < 524288 the robust exhaustive branch of Section 6.8 with 2^26 copies per candidate) has worst-case peak quantum space S_Q(N,s) = O(2^(n/(12 log2 n)) n^38 log2 n) qubits (all Q copies of n+1 qubits are held from acquisition until use, plus O(n) ancillas; S_Q <= (n+1)Q + O(n); proof.md Section 8), i.e. envelope B_Q(n) = 2^(n/(12 log2 n)) n^38 log2 n, whose growth index is exactly 1. This holds on every execution branch, for the clean problem and for every adversary of the error model of the fifth claim, jointly with the other three resource bounds and full-secret success probability at least 9/10 (> 2/3) of the same algorithm and configuration (proof.md Theorems 1 and 2). All constants are absolute (independent of N, s, the adversary and all outcomes); inputs with n < 524288 are finitely many values of N with constant cost.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N) and L = log2 n, the RLS-12L algorithm (robust low-bit sieve with 12 ceil(log2 n) stages) with the single parameter rule of proof.md Section 4 (for n >= 524288: at most R = 12 ceil(log2 n) stages per round, b = ceil((n-1)/R) bits per stage, M = R 2^(b+2R+6) leaves per round, G = 2^(R+9) grid guesses, k = 64 bitlength(100G) test copies per guess, Q = G(nM + k) copies all acquired before the first measurement, r1 = 200 bitlength(1600(n+1)Q), sort keys of 2 bitlength(Q) + 10 bits; for n < 524288 the robust exhaustive branch of Section 6.8 with 2^26 copies per candidate) acquires exactly Q = G(nM + k) source copies on every branch for n >= 524288 (and exactly N 2^26 <= 2^524313 copies, bounded by an absolute constant, for n < 524288), counting every discarded copy and every unused block; for n >= 524288, Q < 2^56 n^37 (log2 n) 2^(n/(12 log2 n)) = O(2^(n/(12 log2 n)) n^37 log2 n) (proof.md Section 8), i.e. the full uniform bound with envelope B_samples(n) = 2^(n/(12 log2 n)) n^37 log2 n, whose growth index is exactly 1, with the same n and success guarantee as the other resources. This holds on every execution branch, for the clean problem and for every adversary of the error model of the fifth claim, jointly with the other three resource bounds and full-secret success probability at least 9/10 (> 2/3) of the same algorithm and configuration (proof.md Theorems 1 and 2). All constants are absolute (independent of N, s, the adversary and all outcomes); inputs with n < 524288 are finitely many values of N with constant cost.

Fractional error tolerance epsilon(n) = 1/16384n^{12}, for every N >= 2 (no validity threshold; n < 524288 is covered by the branch of proof.md Section 6.8) and every s, under the adaptive malformed-copy model of the error_model text (proof.md Section 5): with Q acquired copies at most floor(Q/(16384n^{12})) are malformed; the adversary knows N, s, the algorithm and every measurement outcome obtained before each delivery and chooses adaptively which copies are malformed; malformed copies are arbitrary (n+1)-qubit states, possibly entangled with one another and with the adversary's system but not with clean copies or the algorithm's workspace; every other copy is, at delivery, an independent ideal coset state in tensor product with everything else; the adversary has no access after delivery. For every such adversary, including the one that corrupts nothing (the clean problem), RLS-12L outputs the entire s with probability at least 9/10 (proof.md Theorems 1 and 2), jointly with the four resource bounds of the first four claims, which hold on every branch. The fraction bounds the number of malformed copies among acquired copies; it is not a per-copy corruption probability.

structured.error_model: Adaptive malformed-copy model with fraction epsilon(n). Parameters: N >= 2 is the modulus, s in Z/NZ the secret, n = ceil(log2 N), Q the total number of source copies the algorithm acquires, and epsilon(n) the tolerated malformed fraction. Copies are delivered one at a time in acquisition order j = 1, ..., Q. Before copy j is delivered, an adversary that knows N, s, the full description of the algorithm, and every measurement outcome the algorithm obtained before copy j is delivered, and that may hold, process and measure an arbitrary private quantum system, decides adaptively whether copy j is malformed; on every execution branch at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed. A malformed copy is an arbitrary (n+1)-qubit state (the register shape of an ideal copy) supplied from the adversary's system: it may be pure or mixed, may be entangled with the adversary's remaining system and with other malformed copies, and may depend on all of the information above; it is not entangled with clean copies or with the algorithm's workspace, ancillas or internal random bits. Every copy that is not malformed is clean: at the moment of its delivery, a fresh ideal coset state rho_s = (1/N) sum_x |psi_{x,s}><psi_{x,s}| in tensor product with everything else (the adversary's system, all other copies and the algorithm's workspace), i.e. clean copies are independent ideal coset states. The adversary interacts with the algorithm only by supplying copies; after delivery it has no access to the copy or to the algorithm's quantum or classical systems. All measurements have countably many outcomes. The algorithm is not told which copies are malformed. Quantifiers: the guarantee must hold for every N >= 2 (no validity threshold), every s in Z/NZ and every such adversary, including the adversary that corrupts nothing (the clean problem): the algorithm outputs the entire s with probability at least 2/3, and the four declared resource bounds hold on every execution branch. The fraction bounds the number of malformed copies among acquired copies; it is not a per-copy corruption probability.
